name: W fusion
summary: A W-spider plugged into the input of another W-spider fuses with it.
description:
The W-spider (black triangle) with one input and $n$ outputs maps $|0\rangle \mapsto |0\cdots 0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \mapsto |10\cdots0\rangle + |010\cdots0\rangle + \cdots + |0\cdots01\rangle$: it spreads a single excitation over its outputs in all possible ways. The small dot marks its input leg.

When an output of one W-spider is connected to the input of another, the two fuse into a single W-spider with all the remaining outputs. This expresses (co)associativity of the W-spider, and is the reason we can speak of a single $n$-output W-spider rather than a tree of binary ones.

In Hadzihasanovic's undirected presentation this is the spider rule $\mathrm{sp}_W^{n,m}$ for black vertices: two black vertices connected through a binary black vertex fuse. Together with [W identity](../w-identity/) it also gives the unit law: fusing with a W-spider that has no outputs simply removes an output.
parameter_notes: n is the number of other outputs of the first W-spider and m the number of outputs of the second (shown for n = 1, m = 2); holds for any n and m.

also_in.location: Chapter 5, Section 5.2 (list of rules of the ZW calculus), rule $cut_w$

n.label: other outputs of the first W-spider
